```{r}
detect_records_maxima_norm<-function(X){
  l=length(X)
  rec_max=c(X[1])
  ind_max<-c(1)
  
  for(i in 2:(l-1)){
    #print(i)
    if(X[i-1]<=X[i] && X[i]>X[i+1]){
      l<-length(rec_max)
      if(X[i]> rec_max[l]){
        rec_max<-c(rec_max,X[i])
        ind_max<-c(ind_max,i)
      }
    }
  }
  df<-data.frame(rec_max,ind_max)
  return(df)
}
```

```{r}
statistiques_resumees <- function(traj) {
  increments <- diff(traj)
  c(
    var(increments),
    sd(traj),
    mean(traj),
    max(traj) - min(traj),           # tendance moyenne (pente)
    sd(diff(traj)),                  # volatilité des incréments
    acf(traj, plot = FALSE, lag.max = 1)$acf[2]
  )
}
```

```{r}
roughness_stat <- function(traj, lags = c(1, 2, 4, 8)) {
  n <- length(traj)
  qv <- sapply(lags, function(l) {
    idx <- seq(1, n, by = l)
    sum(diff(traj[idx])^2)
  })
  # pente en log-log ~ related à l'exposant de Hölder/Hurst
  coef(lm(log(qv) ~ log(lags)))[2]
}


statistiques_resumees <- function(traj) {
  increments <- diff(traj)
  c(
    var_incr=var(increments),
    va=var(traj),                          # variance globale
    sd=sd(diff(traj)),                     # écart-type des incréments
    mean=mean(diff(traj)^2),                 # "quadratic variation" empirique
    diff=diff(range(traj)),
    acf1=acf(traj, plot = FALSE, lag.max = 1)$acf[2],
    zero_cross=sum(diff(sign(increments)) != 0),
    hurst=roughness_stat(traj),
    arc_length=sum(sqrt(diff(seq_along(traj))^2 + diff(traj)^2))
  )
}
```

```{r}
# Simule un petit échantillon, regarde la corrélation stat <-> hyperparamètre
N_test <- 1000
SigmaS_v <- runif(N_test, Ssmin,Ssmax)
Sd_v <- runif(N_test, Sdmin,Sdmax)

stats_test <- t(sapply(1:N_test, function(i) {
  traj <- simRecords(dMor_0,
                         N=N,
                         gaussConv = TRUE,
                         sigmaGauss = SigmaS_v[i],
                         sd = Sd_v[i])[,2]
  statistiques_resumees(traj)
}))

# Corrélation entre chaque stat candidate et chaque hyperparamètre
cor(stats_test, cbind(SigmaS_v,Sd_v))
```

```{r}
library(abc)

# 1. Trajectoire observée (celle pour laquelle tu veux estimer les hyperparamètres)
obs_traj <-ts_interp1
obs_summary <- statistiques_resumees(obs_traj)  # ex: moyenne, variance, etc.


sim_summary <- matrix(NA, nrow = n_samples, ncol = length(obs_summary))
for (i in 1:n_samples) {
  traj_sim <-X_bm_NA_corr[i, ]
  sim_summary[i, ] <- statistiques_resumees(traj_sim)
}

# 3. ABC rejection
res <- abc(target = obs_summary,
           param = params_bm_NA_corr,
           sumstat = sim_summary,
           tol = 0.01,          # tolérance : garde les 1% les plus proches
           method = "rejection")  # ou "loclinear" pour une régression locale

summary(res)
hist(res)  # posterior approximé de theta1 et theta2
```
### couplage NN
Lancer le code NBI_NA

```{r}
# Supposons que ton NN est déjà entraîné et chargé, ex: nn_model
# et qu'il prend en entrée une trajectoire (vecteur ou matrice selon ton format)


statistiques_resumees_nn <- function(traj) {
  mask_r <- ifelse(is.na(traj), 0, 1)
  X_real <- ifelse(is.na(traj), 0,traj/C)
  X_real_filled <- matrix(X_real, nrow = 1)
  mask_real     <- matrix(mask_r, nrow = 1)
  # adapte le format d'entrée selon ce qu'attend ton modèle
  # (ex: reshape en matrice 1 x n, normalisation si le NN a été entraîné sur données scalées)
  pred_scaled_bo <- model_BM$predict(list(X_real_filled, mask_real),verbose=0)
  pred_bo <- sweep(pred_scaled_bo, 2, sd, `*`) # dénormalisation
  pred_bo <- sweep(pred_bo, 2, mu, `+`)
  as.numeric(pred_bo)  # c(variance_hat, lissage_hat)
}
```


```{r}
obs_traj <-ts_interp1
obs_summary <- statistiques_resumees_nn(obs_traj)  # ex: moyenne, variance, etc.


sim_summary <- matrix(NA, nrow = n_samples, ncol = length(obs_summary))
for (i in 1:n_samples) {
  print(i)
  traj_sim <-X_bm_NA_corr[i, ]
  sim_summary[i, ] <- statistiques_resumees_nn(traj_sim)
}

# 3. ABC rejection
res <- abc(target = obs_summary,
           param = params_bm_NA_corr,
           sumstat = sim_summary,
           tol = 0.01,          # tolérance : garde les 1% les plus proches
           method = "loclinear")  # ou "loclinear" pour une régression locale

summary(res)
hist(res)  # posterior approximé de theta1 et theta2

# resultats :
```

### Résultat définitif

```{r}
# Simule M trajectoires avec des theta connus (différents de ceux d'entraînement du NN)
M <- 5000
sd_test <- runif(M, Sdmin, Sdmax)
s_test <- runif(M,Ssmin,Ssmax)


resultats <- data.frame(
  sd_vrai = sd_test,s_vrai = s_test,
  sd_nn = NA, s_nn = NA,
  sd_abc = NA, s_abc = NA,
  sd_abc_hybride = NA, s_abc_hybride = NA
)

for (i in 1:M) {
  traj <- simRecords(dMor_0,
                         N=N,
                         gaussConv = TRUE,
                         sigmaGauss = s_test[i],
                         sd = sd_test[i])[,2]
  # NN
  mask_r <- ifelse(is.na(traj), 0, 1)
  X_real <- ifelse(is.na(traj), 0,traj/C)
  X_real_filled <- matrix(X_real, nrow = 1)
  mask_real     <- matrix(mask_r, nrow = 1)
  # adapte le format d'entrée selon ce qu'attend ton modèle
  # (ex: reshape en matrice 1 x n, normalisation si le NN a été entraîné sur données scalées)
  pred_scaled_bo <- model_BM$predict(list(X_real_filled, mask_real),verbose=0)
  pred_bo <- sweep(pred_scaled_bo, 2, sd, `*`) # dénormalisation
  pred_bo <- sweep(pred_bo, 2, mu, `+`)

  pred_nn <- pred_bo
  resultats$sd_nn[i] <- pred_nn[2]
  resultats$s_nn[i] <- pred_nn[1]
  
  # ABC (stats manuelles ou hybride NN)
  obs_summary <- statistiques_resumees_nn(traj)
  res_abc <- abc(target = obs_summary, param = params_bm_NA_corr, sumstat = sim_summary,
                 tol = 0.01, method = "loclinear")
  resultats$sd_abc_hybride[i] <- mean(res_abc$adj.values[,2])
  resultats$s_abc_hybride[i] <- mean(res_abc$adj.values[,1])
}

```

### c) Figure 10
Area and mean of the simulated trajectories with or without the predicted parameters. The black line is the real trajectory of the \textit{Glacier des Bossons}. Blue elements correspond to simulations made with random parameters $\sigma$ and $s$ (chosen according to their prior distribution). Orange elements correspond to simulations made with the parameters predicted by the neural network (presented in table \ref{tab:results_param_bossons}). Transparent areas are the envelopes (see equations \eqref{eq:quantile} and \eqref{eq:fct_dist})  of the simulations and the dotted lines are the mean of the simulations.

### Densités
```{r}
# traj : matrice 1000 x n (lignes = trajectoires, colonnes = temps)
n_traj <- nrow(X_pb_NA_corr)
n_time <- ncol(X_pb_NA_corr)

# Définir les bins de valeurs

val_range <- range(X_pb_NA_corr)
breaks <- seq(val_range[1], val_range[2], length.out = n_bins + 1)
bin_centers <- (breaks[-1] + breaks[-length(breaks)]) / 2

# Matrice densité : n_bins x n_time
dens_mat <- matrix(0, nrow = n_bins, ncol = n_time)

for (t in 1:n_time) {
  h2 <- hist(X_pb_NA_corr[, t], breaks = breaks, plot = FALSE)
  dens_mat[, t] <- h2$counts / n_traj  # normalisation -> densité relative
}


```

```{r}
library(ggplot2)
library(reshape2)

df <- melt(dens_mat)
colnames(df) <- c("bin", "time", "density")
df$value <- bin_centers[df$bin]
df$density[df$density == 0] <- NA

# On regarde la distribution des densités non-nulles pour choisir un seuil
quantile(df$density, probs = c(0.5, 0.9, 0.95, 0.99), na.rm = TRUE)

cap <- quantile(df$density, 0.95, na.rm = TRUE)  # à ajuster selon ce que tu vois

ggplot(df, aes(x = time, y = value, fill = density)) +
  geom_raster() +
  scale_fill_distiller(
    palette = "RdYlBu", 
    trans = "sqrt",
    limits = c(0, cap),
    oob = scales::squish,   # <- clé : écrase (au lieu de mettre NA) tout ce qui dépasse cap
    na.value = "white"
  ) +
  geom_line(data = data.frame(time = 1:n_time, mean = colMeans(X_pb_NA_corr)),
            aes(x = time, y = mean), inherit.aes = FALSE, color = "red") +
    geom_line(data = data.frame(xx=(mor1_0:morf_0)-mor1_0,yy=X_NA[(mor1_0:morf_0)]),

        geom_point(data = data.frame(dMor_0[,1],dMor_0[,2]),
            aes(x = dMor_0[,1]-mor1_0,y=dMor_0[,2]), inherit.aes = FALSE, color = "blue",size=2) +
  theme_minimal() +
```

```{r}

w<- which(!is.na(X_NA[mor1_0:morf_0]))

err_pred <- apply(X_pb_NA_corr[,w], 1,function(x) mse((X_NA[mor1_0:morf_0])[w]  , x))
err_rand <-apply(X_bm_NA_corr[,w], 1,function(x) mse((X_NA[mor1_0:morf_0])[w], x))

w1<-which(err_pred==min(err_pred))

err_rand_MAPE <- apply(X_bm_NA_corr[,w], 1,function(x) MAPE((X_NA[mor1_0:morf_0])[w], x))

aire_mean<-apply(X_pb_NA_corr[,w],1, function(x) trapz(x))
```

### g) Figure 8
Violin plots of the distributions of the 95\% interval of the errors with the predicted parameters or with random ones. Subfigure a) illustrates the MSE  (see Equation \eqref{mse}) and subfigure b) the MAPE (see Equation \eqref{mape}). For both subfigures, the violin plots show the distribution of the error between the real \textit{Glacier des Bossons} trajectory and the predictions. The left violin plots are made on simulations made with random parameters $\sigma$ and $s$ (chosen according to their prior distribution) and the right violin plots are made on simulations made with the parameters predicted by the neural network (presented in Table \ref{tab:results_param_bossons}).

```{r}
M <- 1000
sd_test <- runif(M, Sdmin, Sdmax)
s_test <- runif(M,Ssmin,Ssmax)

resultats2 <- data.frame(
  sd_vrai = sd_test,s_vrai = s_test,
  sd_nn = NA, s_nn = NA,
  sd_abc = NA, s_abc = NA
)

for (i in 1:M) {
  traj <- simRecords(dMor_0,
                         N=N,
                         gaussConv = TRUE,
                         sigmaGauss = s_test[i],
                         sd = sd_test[i])[,2]
  # Méthode 1 : NN seul
  mask_r <- ifelse(is.na(traj), 0, 1)
  X_real <- ifelse(is.na(traj), 0,traj/C)
  X_real_filled <- matrix(X_real, nrow = 1)
  mask_real     <- matrix(mask_r, nrow = 1)
  # adapte le format d'entrée selon ce qu'attend ton modèle
  # (ex: reshape en matrice 1 x n, normalisation si le NN a été entraîné sur données scalées)
  pred_scaled_bo <- model_BM$predict(list(X_real_filled, mask_real),verbose=0)
  pred_bo <- sweep(pred_scaled_bo, 2, sd, `*`) # dénormalisation
  pred_bo <- sweep(pred_bo, 2, mu, `+`)

  pred_nn <- pred_bo
  resultats2$sd_nn[i] <- pred_nn[2]
  resultats2$s_nn[i] <- pred_nn[1]
  
  # Méthode 2 : ABC avec stats du NN
  obs_summary <- statistiques_resumees_nn(traj)
  res_abc <- abc(target = obs_summary, param = params_bm_NA_corr, sumstat = sim_summary,
                 tol = 0.01, method = "loclinear")
  resultats2$sd_abc[i] <- mean(res_abc$adj.values[,2])
  resultats2$s_abc[i] <- mean(res_abc$adj.values[,1])
}
```

```{r}
# x_reel : trajectoire réelle, vecteur de longueur N
# resultats3_ABC, resultats3_NN : matrices M x N

increments <- function(X) {
  if (is.matrix(X)) X[, -1, drop = FALSE] - X[, -ncol(X), drop = FALSE]  
  else diff(X)                                                          
}

inc_reel <- increments(ts_interp1)
inc_ABC  <- increments(resultats3_ABC)
inc_NN   <- increments(resultats3_NN)

# ---------- 1) QQ plot poolé ----------
qqplot_pool <- function(inc_sim, inc_reel, titre, n_q = 200) {
  probs  <- (1:n_q - 0.5) / n_q
  q_sim  <- quantile(as.vector(inc_sim), probs)
  q_reel <- quantile(inc_reel, probs)
  lim <- range(q_sim, q_reel)
  plot(q_sim, q_reel, pch = 16, cex = 0.6, xlim = lim, ylim = lim,
       xlab = "Quantiles simulés", ylab = "Quantiles réels", main = titre)
  abline(0, 1, col = "red", lty = 2)
}

par(mfrow = c(1, 2))
qqplot_pool(inc_ABC, inc_reel, "ABC")
qqplot_pool(inc_NN,  inc_reel, "NN")

# ---------- 2) QQ plot avec enveloppe ----------
qqplot_enveloppe <- function(inc_sim, inc_reel, titre) {
  sim_tri  <- t(apply(inc_sim, 1, sort))            # M x (N-1), tri par ligne
  reel_tri <- sort(inc_reel)
  med <- apply(sim_tri, 2, median)
  lo  <- apply(sim_tri, 2, quantile, probs = 0.025)
  hi  <- apply(sim_tri, 2, quantile, probs = 0.975)

  lim <- range(lo, hi, reel_tri)
  plot(med, reel_tri, type = "n", xlim = lim, ylim = lim,
       xlab = "Quantiles of simulations (median)", ylab = "Quantiles of real trajectory", main = titre)
  polygon(c(med, rev(med)), c(lo, rev(hi)),
          col = rgb(0.5, 0.5, 0.5, 0.3), border = NA)
  points(med, reel_tri, pch = 16, cex = 0.5)
  abline(0, 1, col = "red", lty = 2)
  legend("topleft", legend = c("Real", "95 % simulated CI"),
         pch = c(16, 15), col = c("black", rgb(0.5, 0.5, 0.5, 0.5)), bty = "n")
}

par(mfrow = c(1, 2))
qqplot_enveloppe(inc_ABC, inc_reel, "ABC")
qqplot_enveloppe(inc_NN,  inc_reel, "NN")
par(mfrow = c(1, 1))


# inc_reel, inc_ABC, inc_NN calculés comme avant

# ---------- 1) QQ plot gaussien (poolé pour les simulations) ----------
qqnorm_pool <- function(inc, titre, n_q = 500) {
  x <- as.vector(inc)
  probs <- (1:n_q - 0.5) / n_q
  q_emp <- quantile(x, probs)          # quantiles empiriques
  q_th  <- qnorm(probs)                # quantiles N(0,1)
  plot(q_th, q_emp, pch = 16, cex = 0.6,
       xlab = "Theoretical quantiles N(0,1)",
       ylab = "Empirical quantiles", main = titre)
  # droite passant par les quartiles (robuste aux queues)
  y <- quantile(x, c(0.25, 0.75)); xt <- qnorm(c(0.25, 0.75))
  b <- diff(y) / diff(xt); a <- y[1] - b * xt[1]
  abline(a, b, col = "red", lty = 2)
}

par(mfrow = c(1, 3))
qqnorm_pool(inc_reel, "Réel")
qqnorm_pool(inc_ABC,  "ABC")
qqnorm_pool(inc_NN,   "NN")
par(mfrow = c(1, 1))


qqnorm_env <- function(inc, titre, B = 2000) {
  inc <- as.numeric(inc)
  inc <- inc[is.finite(inc)]
  n <- length(inc)
  z <- sort((inc - mean(inc)) / sd(inc))
  probs <- (1:n - 0.5) / n
  th <- qnorm(probs)

  sims <- replicate(B, sort(rnorm(n)))
  lo <- apply(sims, 1, quantile, probs = 0.025)
  hi <- apply(sims, 1, quantile, probs = 0.975)

  plot(th, z, type = "n", xlim = range(th), ylim = range(lo, hi, z),
       xlab = "N(0,1) quantiles", ylab = "Empirical quantiles", main = titre)
  polygon(c(th, rev(th)), c(lo, rev(hi)), col = rgb(0.5, 0.5, 0.5, 0.3), border = NA)
  points(th, z, pch = 16, cex = 0.5)
  abline(0, 1, col = "red", lty = 2)
}


par(mfrow = c(1, 3))
qqnorm_env(inc_reel, "Real trajectory")
qqnorm_pool(inc_ABC,  "ABC")
qqnorm_pool(inc_NN,   "NN")
par(mfrow = c(1, 1))
```

```{r}
n_inc <- length(inc_reel)                       # 181

qq_segments_env <- function(inc_sim, inc_reel, seg, modele) {
  K <- max(seg)
  par(mfrow = c(2, 4), oma = c(0, 0, 2, 0), mar = c(4, 4, 2, 1))
  for (k in 1:K) {
    idx <- which(seg == k)
    sim_tri  <- t(apply(inc_sim[, idx, drop = FALSE], 1, sort))
    reel_tri <- sort(inc_reel[idx])
    med <- apply(sim_tri, 2, median)
    lo  <- apply(sim_tri, 2, quantile, probs = 0.025)
    hi  <- apply(sim_tri, 2, quantile, probs = 0.975)
    lim <- range(lo, hi, reel_tri)

    plot(med, reel_tri, type = "n", xlim = lim, ylim = lim,
         xlab = "Simulated quantiles (m)", ylab = "Real quantiles (m)",
         main = paste0("Segment ", k, " (t = ", min(idx), "–", max(idx), ")"))
    polygon(c(med, rev(med)), c(lo, rev(hi)),
            col = rgb(0.5, 0.5, 0.5, 0.3), border = NA)
    points(med, reel_tri, pch = 16, cex = 0.6)
    abline(0, 1, col = "red", lty = 2)
  }
  plot.new()
  legend("center", legend = c("Real", "Simulated 95% CI", "y = x"),
         pch = c(16, 15, NA), lty = c(NA, NA, 2),
         col = c("black", rgb(0.5, 0.5, 0.5, 0.5), "red"), bty = "n")
  mtext(paste("QQ plot of increments by segment:", modele),
        outer = TRUE, font = 2, cex = 1.1)
  par(mfrow = c(1, 1), oma = c(0, 0, 0, 0), mar = c(5, 4, 4, 2) + 0.1)
}



qqnorm_env_seg <- function(inc, seg, titre, B = 2000) {
  K <- max(seg)
  par(mfrow = c(2, 4), oma = c(0, 0, 2, 0), mar = c(4, 4, 2, 1))
  for (k in 1:K) {
    x <- inc[seg == k]
    x <- x[is.finite(x)]
    n <- length(x)
    z <- sort((x - mean(x)) / sd(x))
    th <- qnorm((1:n - 0.5) / n)
    sims <- replicate(B, sort(rnorm(n)))
    lo <- apply(sims, 1, quantile, probs = 0.025)
    hi <- apply(sims, 1, quantile, probs = 0.975)

    plot(th, z, type = "n", xlim = range(th), ylim = range(lo, hi, z),
         xlab = "N(0,1) quantiles", ylab = "Empirical quantiles",
         main = paste("Segment", k))
    polygon(c(th, rev(th)), c(lo, rev(hi)), col = rgb(0.5, 0.5, 0.5, 0.3), border = NA)
    points(th, z, pch = 16, cex = 0.6)
    abline(0, 1, col = "red", lty = 2)
  }
  mtext(titre, outer = TRUE, font = 2, cex = 1.1)
  par(mfrow = c(1, 1), oma = c(0, 0, 0, 0), mar = c(5, 4, 4, 2) + 0.1)
}




qqnorm_pool_seg <- function(inc_sim, seg, titre, n_q = 300) {
  K <- max(seg)
  par(mfrow = c(2, 4), oma = c(0, 0, 2, 0), mar = c(4, 4, 2, 1))
  probs <- (1:n_q - 0.5) / n_q
  for (k in 1:K) {
    x <- as.vector(inc_sim[, seg == k])
    z <- (x - mean(x)) / sd(x)
    plot(qnorm(probs), quantile(z, probs), pch = 16, cex = 0.5,
         xlab = "N(0,1) quantiles", ylab = "Empirical quantiles",
         main = paste("Segment", k))
    abline(0, 1, col = "red", lty = 2)
  }
  mtext(titre, outer = TRUE, font = 2, cex = 1.1)
  par(mfrow = c(1, 1), oma = c(0, 0, 0, 0), mar = c(5, 4, 4, 2) + 0.1)
}

qq_segments_both <- function(inc_ABC, inc_NN, inc_reel, seg,
                             col_ABC = "#D55E00", col_NN = "#0072B2",
                             bande = TRUE) {
  K <- max(seg)
  par(mfrow = c(2, 4), oma = c(0, 0, 2, 0), mar = c(4, 4, 2, 1))

  # fonction interne : médiane et bornes 95 % des stats d'ordre
  stats_ordre <- function(inc_sim, idx) {
    tri <- t(apply(inc_sim[, idx, drop = FALSE], 1, sort))
    list(med = apply(tri, 2, median),
         lo  = apply(tri, 2, quantile, probs = 0.025),
         hi  = apply(tri, 2, quantile, probs = 0.975))
  }

  for (k in 1:K) {
    idx  <- which(seg == k)
    reel <- sort(inc_reel[idx])
    A <- stats_ordre(inc_ABC, idx)
    N <- stats_ordre(inc_NN,  idx)
    lim <- range(A$lo, A$hi, N$lo, N$hi, reel)

    plot(A$med, reel, type = "n", xlim = lim, ylim = lim,
         xlab = "Simulated quantiles (m)", ylab = "Real quantiles (m)",
         main = paste0("Segment ", k, " (t = ", min(idx), "–", max(idx), ")"))
    if (bande) {
      polygon(c(A$med, rev(A$med)), c(A$lo, rev(A$hi)),
              col = adjustcolor(col_ABC, 0.15), border = NA)
      polygon(c(N$med, rev(N$med)), c(N$lo, rev(N$hi)),
              col = adjustcolor(col_NN, 0.15), border = NA)
    }
    abline(0, 1, col = "grey30", lty = 2)
    points(A$med, reel, pch = 16, cex = 0.7, col = col_ABC)
    points(N$med, reel, pch = 17, cex = 0.7, col = col_NN)
  }

  plot.new()
  legend("center",
         legend = c("ABC/NN", "NN", "y = x"),
         pch = c(16, 17, NA), lty = c(NA, NA, 2),
         col = c(col_ABC, col_NN, "grey30"), bty = "n", cex = 1.1)
  mtext("QQ plots of increments by segment: real vs simulated (ABC/NN and NN)",
        outer = TRUE, font = 2, cex = 1.1)
  par(mfrow = c(1, 1), oma = c(0, 0, 0, 0), mar = c(5, 4, 4, 2) + 0.1)
}

qq_segments_both(inc_ABC, inc_NN, inc_reel, seg)
```

```{r}
metriques <- function(pred, vrai) {
  err <- pred - vrai
  c(
    biais = mean(err),
    rmse  = sqrt(mean(err^2)),
    mae   = mean(abs(err)),
    cor   = cor(pred, vrai)
  )
}
```

```{r}
coverage_95 <- sapply(1:M, function(i) {
  traj <- simRecords(dMor_0,
                         N=N,
                         gaussConv = TRUE,
                         sigmaGauss = s_test[i],
                         sd = sd_test[i])[,2]
  obs_summary <- statistiques_resumees_nn(traj)
  res_abc <- abc(target = obs_summary, param = params_bm_NA_corr, sumstat = sim_summary,
                 tol = 0.05, method = "loclinear")  # tol un peu plus large pour un intervalle stable
  ci <- quantile(res_abc$adj.values[,1], c(0.025, 0.975))
  s_test[i] >= ci[1] & s_test[i] <= ci[2]
})
```

```{r}
  geom_abline(slope = 1, intercept = 0, linetype = "dashed", color = '#D1C700') +
  labs(title = "ABC-hybrid",x = "True sigma", y = "Estimated sigma") +
  theme_minimal()

p_nn + p_abc
```
